rejected_answer.headline: Your profile has no branch format, budget, or opening date, and curated evidence gives no staffing ratios or wages — here is a compliance-anchored setup skeleton plus the two missing inputs.

items.text: Dubai delivery handling guidance (still linked as of the 2026-10-12 check, though flagged for review) requires sealed containers and hot/cold separation in insulated secondary units, and transport holding at 60 C or above for hot food and 5 C or below for cold.

In Abu Dhabi, ADAFSA describes Essential Food Safety Training for food handlers and periodic operator self-inspections using an approved checklist with documented findings, corrective actions, and follow-up records available to inspectors.

Observed extended-hours operators show night trading exists in these markets, but branch listings of Zaroob (Marina 7 AM-5 AM; SZR and Motor City 24-hour) and Allo Beirut (Hessa Street delivery until 4 AM; Khalifa City 8 AM-12:30 AM) do not establish overnight demand or a required roster.
No curated observation establishes salary levels, headcount per shift, labour-cost ratios, kitchen equipment counts, or a staffing requirement for a meaty-pizza/kebab-sandwich format.

Dubai: propose one compact production line — a kebab grill/slicer station and a pizza oven station — plus separate packaging and a dispatch shelf. This fits the combo menu without asserting a specific equipment spec; confirm gas/electrical load, extraction, and municipality approval on the chosen site.

Abu Dhabi: branches such as Papa Johns in Al Zahiyah, Khalidiya, Al Manhal and Allo Beirut in Al Danah, Khalifa City show the format distributes across both mall-adjacent and neighbourhood streets, so propose the same core line with a smaller front-of-house footprint and pickup shelf in a neighbourhood site. Treat mall versus street choice as a site-check decision, not a settled one.

For both cities, propose a role set rather than headcount: one manager/owner-operator carrying ADAFSA/Dubai Municipality training records, two to three cross-trained kitchen staff (grill and oven), one packer/dispatch lead, and one delivery-own-rider only if your order mix justifies it. Name each role, not numbers, until you have measured order volumes.

Propose a written daily routine covering temperature checks, sealed-container dispatch, hot/cold separation, and a completed self-inspection log — checklists you can hold from day one in Abu Dhabi and mirror in Dubai.

sections.title: What to set before we size anything

items.text: Your startup budget, monthly rent budget, branch format, positioning and planned opening are all still unset, so no staffing level or operating cost can be sized reliably from this profile.

The operating model you pick (cloud kitchen, counter, or dine-in) is the single biggest driver of role mix; propose capping one Dubai and one Abu Dhabi site in a single pilot window so a shared core team can cover both until volumes are measured.

assumptions: The restaurant is a Jordan-origin meaty-pizza and kebab-sandwich concept (from your profile).
Branch format, budget, positioning and opening date remain unknown, so this answer gives setup logic, not a sized roster.
next_steps: Use /set to lock startup_budget_aed, monthly_rent_budget_aed, branch_format, positioning and planned_opening — staffing can only be sized against these.
Request a written staffing and operating-cost quote from two kitchen-equipment suppliers and compare delivery versus pickup share assumptions.
Walk two candidate sites per city (one mall-adjacent, one neighbourhood street) and record extraction capacity, gas/electrical supply, and dispatch space before committing to a roster.
